title: A route to the thermodynamics of colloid-polymer mixtures from structural information
authors: Vikki Anand Varma, Andrew J. Archer, Alberto Scacchi
abstract: Liquid-state theory provides a fundamental connection between microscopic structure and macroscopic thermodynamic behaviour. Here, we develop a framework for predicting thermodynamics and phase behaviour directly from structural correlations, using either radial distribution functions or static structure factors as input. The approach constructs a free-energy functional from structural information obtained at a single thermodynamic state point, without requiring explicit knowledge of the underlying interaction potentials. This circumvents a central difficulty in modelling complex fluids, for which effective interactions are often unknown or rely on approximations. We demonstrate the framework for a range of model fluids, including colloidal and colloid--polymer systems, with predictions in good agreement with molecular simulation data. The results show that structural information at a single state point can provide sufficient information to predict the broader thermodynamic response of a system. This establishes a route toward inferring phase behaviour directly from experimentally measured structure, even when the microscopic interactions are not known a priori.
summary: This work presents a powerful theoretical framework to calculate the thermodynamics and phase behavior of complex fluids, such as colloid-polymer mixtures, using only structural data obtained at one state point. By decomposing the free energy into reference (excluded-volume) and tail components, the authors bypass the need to know the underlying interaction potentials. This establishes a crucial link between measurable structural properties and macroscopic phase transitions.
main_problem: The paper develops a framework to predict the thermodynamics and phase behavior of complex fluids, specifically colloid-polymer mixtures, directly from structural correlations.
main_result: It successfully demonstrates that structural information measured at a single state point is sufficient to construct the free energy functional and predict phase coexistence, bypassing the need for explicit interaction potentials.
method: The approach constructs the excess free energy by decomposing interactions into a reference (excluded-volume) part and a tail part, using structural inputs like the radial distribution function or direct correlation function.
model_or_system: The focus is on colloid-polymer mixtures and general fluid systems. The theory is built upon decomposing the total potential into a reference hard-sphere part and a remaining interaction tail, which is then analyzed using integral equation theory concepts.
key_observables: Radial distribution functions (g(r)), static structure factors (S(k)), and the pair direct correlation function (c(r)).
important_parameters: Effective hard-sphere diameter (sigma_opt), inverse temperature (beta), and the integrated attraction strength (A).
main_assumptions: The method assumes radial symmetry for interactions and relies on approximations like Fundamental Measure Theory (FMT) for the reference free energy and the Ornstein-Zernike equation closures.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the predicted binodal curve for a binary mixture and show the reconstruction of pair potentials from structural correlations.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the general theory by decomposing the free energy, details the calculation routes (Thermodynamic Integration, DCF route, Virial route), and applies the framework sequentially to one-component systems before extending it to binary colloid-polymer mixtures to predict phase coexistence.
why_interesting: While focused on classical fluids, the methodology of inferring macroscopic thermodynamic behavior (like phase boundaries) solely from single-point structural measurements is a powerful concept applicable to many-body quantum systems where direct potential knowledge is difficult.
